bars.label: Cold
bars.note: No place on Earth reaches the target value; scored against the closest places on Earth

breaks.text: Cold: the target is −203 °C; the closest anywhere on Earth is −45.4 °C
About 0.17 g on the Moon versus 1 g on Earth
Essentially a vacuum: no wind, no weathering by air, no air to carry heat
No thick air and no global magnetic field to shield the surface
54 °C in sunlight to −203 °C in shadowed craters (NASA Moon Base page); Earth’s record low is about −89 °C

tests: Field-test ground-penetrating radar over buried ice
Rehearse drilling and sample handling in frozen ground
Check thermal models of where ice survives near the surface
